package_info.package_name: Unknown (Any npm package with a hijackable maintainer email domain)
package_info.package_versions: Any version published after maintainer account hijack
package_info.why_malicious: The package becomes malicious when an attacker hijacks a maintainer account via expired email domain, allowing them to publish new versions containing arbitrary malicious code. This enables software supply chain attacks at scale.

execution_context.file_location: Any file in the npm package (e.g., index.js, postinstall script, etc.)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads sensitive files (e.g., /etc/passwd) and exfiltrates their contents via HTTP POST to an attacker-controlled domain, enabling credential or data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs unauthorized access to sensitive files and sends data to an external server during package installation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages should not access or exfiltrate sensitive system files or perform network requests during installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may perform network requests to download dependencies, but never to exfiltrate local files.
key_indicators: Network requests to untrusted domains in install scripts
Access to sensitive files (e.g., /etc/passwd, environment variables)
Data exfiltration during install or import

attack_chain.action: Attacker purchases expired domain associated with a maintainer's email.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to receive password reset emails for the maintainer account.

attack_chain.action: Attacker resets the npm maintainer account password using the hijacked email.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full control over the maintainer account.

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes a new version of the package containing malicious code (e.g., in postinstall script).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is distributed to all users installing or updating the package.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes on user systems, exfiltrating data or performing other attacks.
attack_chain.leads_to: Compromise of user systems and potential lateral movement.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected network requests during npm package installation
Access to sensitive files or environment variables in install/import scripts
New or modified maintainer accounts with recently registered or suspicious email domains
file_indicators: Presence of suspicious postinstall scripts in package.json
References to external domains in JavaScript or shell scripts
Unusual changes in package maintainers or email addresses
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains not associated with the package's legitimate functionality
Connections to newly registered or low-reputation domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages that have recently changed maintainers or maintainer email domains, especially if the domain was recently registered. Analyze package.json scripts for network activity or file access during install/import. Flag packages that attempt to access sensitive files or make outbound network requests to untrusted domains during installation or runtime.
